authoredFrom: ER-D46 (2026-10-23), authored from the part_of CONTRACT in src/ast/types.ts + validation/m14/verification/VOCABULARY-EXTENSION-PROPOSAL.md §2.4, before running the analyzer on this source. The construct: `-include("x.hrl")` / `-include_lib("kernel/…")` is FILE INCLUSION — the header is spliced into this module's single compilation scope, cannot be compiled as a unit of its own, and imports nothing — which is the vocabulary's `part_of` (the same construct php's include/require and fsharp's #load were relabelled to). Direction is the directive's own: source = the file carrying the directive, target = the path as written, and `metadata.partRole` is MANDATORY on every row: "library" here because this file is the including library and names the part. The negative half is the point: the old `references` rows must NOT survive the relabel, an include must NOT be published as `imports` (that is `-import`'s label, ER-D41), and the `-import` module must NOT become a `part_of`. Four directives are exercised — the two legal forms, a SPLIT directive (the line-contract: the path STRING's line, not the keyword's), and an include inside a conditional-compilation region.

expectRelationships.note: plain -include: the directive IS the syntax, so confidence 1.0 and the import_based tier follow the construct (ER-D46)
-include_lib: same part_of relation; the code-path/external classification lives on the ImportInfo entry (ER-D20) and does not change the relation
M59 #825 line contract: the path STRING's line (11), never the -include keyword's line (10)
an include inside -ifdef is still a top-level form in this grammar (pp_ifdef is a leaf sibling), so it is still one part_of row

forbidRelationships.note: ER-D46 negative half: no references row for an include at any line
ER-D46: an include is NOT an import; the imports label belongs to -import (ER-D41)
the -import module is a name import, never a file inclusion — `part_of` must not be borrowed for it

ER-D46 negative control: a file inclusion is not inheritance. TYPE-ONLY, the strongest form — no extends edge may exist in this file, whatever its endpoints, which is what catches the `ontology/extends-from-include` mutant after the label moved to part_of.
ER-D46 negative control: an include does not redefine a member (overrides is ruled grammar-absence for Erlang; see the spec).
